steps.say: Let Claude Code on your laptop press {product}'s buttons for you, for tests and demos, while sign-ins and payments stay with people.
Claude Code on your laptop sends your owner key with every call. {product} checks that the key is still yours, then presses the same buttons you would.
Your key lives here. {product} keeps only its fingerprint and its last four characters, never the key itself.
Click Make my key. The key appears once, inside the one line you paste on your laptop. A new key stops the old one at once.
Paste that line in a terminal on your laptop. Then ask Claude Code to check {product} status.
Every tool is one of your own buttons, checked as you. Search finds a tool even when misspelt.
Signing in, passwords, accepting permissions and payments stay with people. Claude is told which step is next, and never tries it.
